title: Build a QA Checklist from Real Failure Modes
subtitle: Make required checks explicit, observable, and easy to update.
description: Turn a recurring QA task into a short checklist with clear expected results, exception handling, an owner, and a revision step when reality exposes a missing check.

lifeOsSource.hack: Write checklist items around failures that matter, with an observable result for each step and a clear path when a check fails.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Choose one recurring QA activity, list the failure modes that would matter, turn each necessary check into an action plus expected result, define what to capture when the result differs, run the checklist on real work, and revise it when a new recurring miss appears.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Which check changed the release or review decision, which item was ambiguous, and what should be added, removed, or rewritten before the next run?

faq.question: Should a checklist contain every possible QA step?
faq.answer: No. Put the checks needed for this task and its important failure modes in the checklist. Move detailed procedures into a runbook when they would make the checklist hard to scan.

faq.question: What happens when a check fails?
faq.answer: Record the observed result, stop or contain the affected action when the workflow requires it, and follow the defined exception or escalation path rather than marking the step complete.

intro.html: A QA checklist is useful when it turns an important expectation into something a person can actually verify. It should support judgment, not replace it. Start from the failures that matter, state the expected result, and make exceptions visible.

sections.title: 1. Start with failure modes
sections.html: Choose one recurring QA activity and ask what could be missed, misconfigured, stale, incomplete, or inconsistent. Keep only failure modes that would change a decision or create meaningful rework.

sections.title: 2. Write observable checks
sections.html: Use an action and an expected result: open the artifact, run the named check, compare the expected and actual state, and capture enough context to reproduce a failure. Avoid items such as verify everything is OK.

sections.title: 3. Define the exception path
sections.html: For checks that can block release or handoff, state what happens when the result differs: stop, quarantine, investigate, escalate, or obtain an explicit exception. A green checkbox must not hide an unresolved anomaly.

sections.title: 4. Revise from real misses
sections.html: After the run, inspect ambiguity, duplicate work, false alarms, and escaped defects. Change the checklist only when the change makes the next decision clearer or catches a recurring class of failure.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace fabricated release observations, unsupported defect-rate claims, rigid checklist-size rules, and invented benchmarks with a bounded QA execution protocol.
